D018-D005_h001.question:
I’ve been running my restaurant for twelve years, and up until six months ago, I could handle the stress—long hours, managing staff, keeping my husband happy. But lately, little things set me off. A car backfiring outside sent me to the floor last week, trembling. I can’t focus during dinner rush anymore—orders get mixed up because I lose track mid-sentence. 

I don’t feel joy anymore. Not with my husband, not with anything. I’m angry all the time, like there’s a fire under my skin. I keep thinking it was my fault—what happened during that armed robbery last year. I didn’t fight back. I froze. Now I punish myself every day for it.

But what’s worse—what I can’t explain—is the voices. They come out of nowhere, not tied to the robbery. One hisses insults about me being worthless, another argues with me when I’m alone in the kitchen. They don’t replay the trauma—they attack me, accuse me, tell me people are watching. I know it sounds crazy, but they’re not echoes of that night. They’re separate. And they’ve been getting louder.
D018-D005_h001.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h002.question: I’ve been forgetting things constantly—like where I left my keys or even entire sections of my thesis notes—and I can’t focus long enough to edit my drafts. Loud sounds, like a door slamming in the lab, make me jerk so hard I’ve spilled coffee on my papers. It’s like my body’s always braced for something. Ever since the accident last year—when my best friend died in the crash—I get this overwhelming wave of dread if I see a red car like the one that hit us. I hate feeling this way, and I keep thinking it was the driver’s fault, even though I wasn’t there. I can’t enjoy anything now—my defense, seeing friends, even coffee—nothing feels good anymore. I’m just… numb. But what’s scaring me most is that I’ve been hearing voices when no one’s around—usually whispering about me in the next room. They don’t talk about the crash. They say things like “She’s being watched” or “They’re lying about her research.” I haven’t told anyone because I don’t know if it’s stress or something worse. The thoughts feel separate from the trauma—they’re just… there, all the time.
D018-D005_h002.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h003.question: I’ve been struggling for over a year now—maybe longer. It started after a fire in the kitchen, something I still replay constantly: the flames, the screams, the guilt that I didn’t act faster. I keep reliving it, out of nowhere. Sometimes I see the same chef’s jacket burning in front of me, even when I’m not at work. But then, other times, I hear voices—voices that have nothing to do with the fire. They talk about me, mock me, tell me I’m worthless. They’re always there, even in quiet moments at home with my wife. That’s not a flashback—that’s something else. I can’t feel joy anymore. I don’t laugh. I don’t connect. I feel dead inside, like I’ve failed everyone. I blame myself for what happened, but now I also think people are watching me, plotting. My mind feels foggy, like I’m moving through water. And if someone touches me unexpectedly, I jolt like I’ve been shocked. It’s like my body’s always braced for disaster—both the one I lived through and the one I keep hearing about in those voices. The voices aren’t memories. They’re new. And they’re real to me.
D018-D005_h003.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h004.question:
I’ve been a speech therapist for over ten years, so I notice when my thoughts start slipping out of order—words not connecting right, ideas spiraling. For the past eight months, I keep reliving the car accident—sudden flashes of twisted metal, the smell of fuel, my husband’s voice screaming. They hit me out of nowhere, and I can’t shake them. I used to love cooking for my family, but now I don’t care. Nothing feels meaningful. I even stopped seeing my closest clients—I just couldn’t trust myself to stay focused.

What’s scarier, though, are the voices. Not during the flashbacks—after. I’ll be lying in bed, and I hear my mother’s voice, but she died years ago. She’s accusing me, saying I caused the crash, that I’m broken. It’s not like the memories—it’s like she’s really there. Sometimes I see shadows moving in the hallway, whispering about me. I can’t decide what to wear anymore; even picking toast or cereal feels impossible. And if a door slams, my heart races for twenty minutes—I don’t come down easily.

I know some of this is from the trauma, but these voices, these visions—they don’t reenact the crash. They’re separate. And they’re relentless.
D018-D005_h004.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h005.question:
I’ve been struggling for about six months now, ever since that night when I found my roommate after… well, after he took his own life. I keep having these awful dreams where I’m back in that moment—his voice calling out, the phone ringing endlessly. I wake up drenched in sweat, heart pounding. It’s not just the dreams, though. I can’t enjoy anything anymore—not gaming, not music, not even hanging out with friends. I just feel numb. I keep thinking, *I should’ve checked on him*, *I could’ve stopped it*. The guilt eats at me every single day.

But lately, things have gotten… stranger. I’ll be coding at work and hear someone clearly say my name from across the room—no one’s there. Once, I even heard a coworker criticizing me, but no one had spoken. It’s not like the dreams—it’s not tied to what happened. And sometimes I get this overwhelming sense that my thoughts are being broadcasted, like others can read my mind. I can’t focus; I keep forgetting where I put my keys, my phone. A car horn the other day made me jump so hard I nearly fell out of my chair. These voices and thoughts? They’re not memories—they’re new, and they scare me more than the past.
D018-D005_h005.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bulimia Nervosa
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h006.question:
I’ve been having these flashes—sudden images of my father yelling, the way he looked that night he died. Even now, if someone raises their voice, my chest tightens and I feel like I can’t breathe. I don’t like talking about it. Sometimes I remember pieces—his face, the broken glass—but other parts just… aren’t there. It’s like my mind blocked them out. I don’t feel much anymore. My husband says I’m distant. I love him, but I just can’t *feel* it.  

I get irritable easily—snapping at coworkers over small things, even though I’ve always prided myself on being precise and calm. If someone walks into my office suddenly, I jolt like I’ve been shocked.  

But that’s not all. Lately, I’ve been hearing my dead brother’s voice, even though he wasn’t there that night. He says things—nonsense about numbers, taxes—stuff I’d never imagine him caring about. Sometimes I see shadows moving in corners, people who aren’t there. These voices and images? They’re not flashbacks. They’re not about the trauma at all. And they’ve been going on for over a year now. It’s like my mind is breaking in two.
D018-D005_h006.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h007.question:
I’ve been struggling for over a year now, ever since that attack downtown—someone came out of an alley and assaulted me. I keep reliving it—sometimes I’m in a client’s office and suddenly I see him again, right in front of me, like it’s happening all over. I shut down, can’t speak, can barely move. I avoid talking about it, even with my husband. I don’t want to feel anything about it… honestly, I don’t want to feel much at all. I can’t even hug my mom like I used to.  

But it’s not just the trauma stuff. Lately, I’ve been hearing voices—clear as you are now—three men arguing about me, saying I’m dangerous, plotting against me. They weren’t there during the assault. They don’t talk about it at all. My husband says I shout at nothing, get angry over small things, like he moved the coffee cup wrong. I jump when people walk into rooms fast.  

I thought it was just the trauma, but the things I hear… they’re not memories. They’re new. And constant. Like my mind isn’t mine anymore.
D018-D005_h007.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h008.question:
I’ve been having these dreams—over and over—dancing on stage, the lights, the fall… I can’t forget the sound of my leg snapping. I wake up sweating, heart racing for what feels like hours. I try not to think about it during the day, but sometimes I do, and it just shuts me down. I can’t feel anything, not even when my boyfriend holds me. I love him, I think, but it’s like something’s been carved out. I yelled at a dancer last week for bumping into me—just screamed, cursed her out—and I didn’t even recognize my own voice. It’s like I’m always braced for impact.  

But… there’s more. Lately, I hear voices when no one’s there—whispers in the studio, saying I’m broken, that I’ll never dance again. They don’t talk about the fall. They just follow me, commenting, laughing. Sometimes I see shadows moving in the mirrors, even when the room's empty. I know they’re not real, but they feel real. It’s not like the memories—it’s something else. I’m not just haunted by the past. I’m losing grip on what’s now.
D018-D005_h008.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h009.question:
I’ve been struggling a lot lately—ever since that mugging last year, I can’t seem to get back to who I was. There are days I don’t remember whole parts of what happened during the attack, like my mind just blanks out. Sometimes I’m standing in the middle of a scene at an audition and suddenly I’m back there—seeing the alley, feeling the hands on me, like it’s happening all over again. It’s terrifying. I try not to think about it, but even certain sounds or shadows make me jump. I’ve thrown water bottles, once even shoved a casting assistant when they came up behind me too fast.

But that’s not all. Lately, I’ve been hearing voices—two men arguing in my apartment when no one’s there. They don’t talk about the mugging, though. They comment on my clothes, say I’m being watched. I see figures in doorways too, vanishing when I turn. I don’t feel much anymore, like I’m just going through motions. My agent says I’m disconnected. I know this sounds crazy, but the voices? They’re not part of the flashback. They’re separate. And they’ve been here longer than the memories ever were.
D018-D005_h009.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)

D018-D005_h010.question:
I’ve been having these terrifying flashbacks—like I’m back in that car crash all over again, smelling the smoke, hearing the crunch of metal. It’s so real I sometimes jump out of my chair, and afterward my heart races for ages. I avoid driving or even riding in cars if I can help it. I remember parts of the accident clearly—the red light, the truck speeding toward me—but whole chunks are just gone. 

It’s not just the trauma stuff, though. Lately, I’ve been hearing voices when no one’s around—two men arguing about me, saying I’m worthless or that I’m being watched. They aren’t part of the flashback; they’re just *there*, even when I’m calm. I snapped at my wife last week and threw a lamp—it scared me how fast it happened. I used to feel proud closing a big sale, but now, nothing feels satisfying. 

The voices don’t talk about the crash. They talk about *me*, like I’m part of some conspiracy. I don’t know if they’re real, but they’re not memories—this feels like something else entirely.
D018-D005_h010.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)
    D. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h011.question:
I’ve been the head nurse at a city hospital for over two decades, so I know mental health well, but lately… I can’t even trust my own mind. I keep *seeing* things—voices talking to me, sometimes entire conversations I didn’t have. Just yesterday in the med room, I heard my ex-husband’s voice, clear as day, saying he was going to ruin me—except he’s been out of my life for ten years. It wasn’t a memory. It felt real, like he was standing right there. And it happens all the time, not just voices—once, I saw shadows moving in the corners of rooms, watching me. 

The flashbacks are bad too—I’ll be charting and suddenly I’m back in that ER from 1995, the night of the mass shooting. I smell the blood, hear the screams. I bolt out of rooms. I avoid the east wing now. But the difference is, even when I’m not in a flashback, the voices are still there, accusing me, or warning me. I yell back sometimes—nurses have had to calm me down. I believe the world’s out to get me. My ex ruined everything, that’s why I’m like this. But these hallucinations… they don’t just replay the trauma. They’re new, unreal things. And they never stop.
D018-D005_h011.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h012.question:
I’ve been having these awful moments where I suddenly feel like I’m back in that burning house—smell the smoke, hear the flames crackling, and I can’t move. My daughter says I stare off and don’t respond. After my husband passed, I stopped going to church, even though I used to love it, because passing the fire station makes me tremble. I keep thinking the world’s turned cruel and nobody can be trusted. I should’ve called the fire department sooner that night—I carry that every day.

But lately, things have gotten worse. I hear voices when no one’s around—sometimes a man whispering that I’m evil, other times laughing at me from the corner. Last week, I threw my teacup across the room because I saw shadows crawling in the walls. These voices don’t sound like anything from the fire—they’re about things that never happened, accusing me of crimes I didn’t commit. I see people standing in the hallway who aren’t there. The flashbacks scare me, yes, but these voices and visions? They’re separate—like another layer entirely.
D018-D005_h012.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h013.question:
I’ve been struggling for years, ever since my divorce turned really messy—there was physical danger, things I don’t like to talk about. Even now, just a tone of voice or someone standing too close can make my chest tighten and my hands shake, like I’m right back there. I try not to think about it—I avoid old neighborhoods, certain conversations—but it still creeps in. I’ve started believing the world is just full of people waiting to hurt you. I blame myself sometimes, like I should’ve left sooner or handled things differently.

Lately, though, things have changed. I hear voices—clear as yours—commenting on what I’m doing, even when no one’s around. They aren’t talking about the trauma. They call me “weak” or argue about random things, like whether I should take a listing. It’s not flashbacks—it’s like strangers in my head. I’ve yelled at them, thrown a tablet once when the voices got loud. My assistant noticed and was scared. This isn’t just reacting to the past. These thoughts feel outside me, and they’ve been getting harder to ignore for over a year now.
D018-D005_h013.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h014.question:
I’ve been struggling for over a year now—since the accident. I keep seeing the same car crash in my head, and even small things like a honking horn or the smell of gasoline send my heart racing, drenched in sweat. I don’t talk about it, not even with my wife. I just push it down. I can’t stand thinking about it—feels like I’m blaming myself for not being in the passenger seat, for not doing anything. Now everything seems dangerous. People? The world? It’s all just out to get you. Life doesn’t even feel real sometimes.

But that’s not all. Lately, I’ve been hearing voices—sharp, angry tones, even when no one’s there. They talk about me, call me “worthless,” say I don’t belong. It’s not the crash they’re describing—it’s like they know things no one does. Sometimes I see shadows moving in my office, even when the lights are on. I threw a chair last week during a meeting—just snapped when someone laughed. My wife says I’m not the same. The thoughts… they don’t feel like mine. They’re separate. Like someone’s feeding them into my head. The voices weren’t there during the trauma. They’re new. And they won’t stop.

D018-D005_h015.question:
I’ve been having these flashes—sudden, vivid memories of the explosion at the restaurant six months ago. I see the flames, hear the screams, feel the heat. They pop up out of nowhere, and I can’t shut them off. I try not to think about it, but the more I avoid it, the more guilty I feel. I should’ve stopped it. I was right there. I keep telling myself the world doesn’t care, that nothing matters if something like that can happen for no reason.

I’ve been snapping at people—my wife, the line cooks—yelling over tiny mistakes. I can’t help it. But lately… it’s not just memories. I hear voices when no one’s around. One sounds like my captain yelling orders, but he never talked like that. Another tells me I’m dangerous, that I’ll burn everything I touch. They say it even when I’m home, when I’m alone. It’s not the fire, not a memory. It feels separate—like they’re watching me, judging me for surviving.  

I don’t know what’s real anymore. The voices don’t come from the trauma—they add to it, twist it. I’m not just reliving it. I’m losing my grip on what’s me and what’s not.
D018-D005_h015.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Schizophrenia
    D. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h016.question:
I’ve been having these flashes—sudden memories of the accident at the concert venue last year. Equipment fell, and someone got hurt. I can’t stop seeing it. I avoid talking about it, even changed studios so I wouldn’t run into people from that job. I keep thinking the lead technician cut corners—he’s to blame. I’m always on edge, scanning the room, checking exits, watching for loose cables or anything that could go wrong.  

But… there’s more. Lately, I’ve been hearing voices when no one’s around. Not like echoes of the event—completely new voices. A man arguing with me about sound levels, a woman whispering during silence, like they’re in the booth with me. They’re not part of the memory. They tell me things, like I messed up a mix that doesn’t exist. Sometimes I feel like people on the street are sending me signals through their headphones.  

It’s been over six months, and the anxiety feels like one thing, but the voices and the paranoia… they came out of nowhere and don’t connect to the accident. I know that sounds strange, but they feel separate—like something else is going on inside my head.
D018-D005_h016.options:
A. Acute Stress Disorder

D018-D005_h017.question:
I’ve been struggling for years—ever since the explosion at the plant. I wasn’t even supposed to be on that shift, but I switched for a coworker. My wife says I’ve changed—talk to myself, jump at air. The thoughts… they don’t feel like mine sometimes. The trauma’s real, but this? It’s like something else has taken hold—something that doesn’t just bring back the past, but lives in the present with me.

D018-D005_h018.question:
